source_or_privileged_boundary: A collaborator or synced archive controls a filename containing a multibyte Unicode scalar in a position the operator intended to exclude with a one-character ? pattern.

title: byte-oriented question-mark globs bypass Unicode names

attack_path_facts.title: byte-oriented question-mark globs bypass Unicode names
attack_steps: The operator defines a one-character .kcsignore rule such as ?.txt and relies on it as an exclusion boundary.
A lower-trust scope contributor supplies a direct child whose one visible character occupies multiple UTF-8 bytes.
The question-mark matcher advances one byte, so the Unicode path does not match while an ASCII peer does.
The file becomes eligible for archive ingestion, normalization, and—when separately approved—online OCR or embedding despite the declared exclusion.
assumptions: A local content contributor can control direct-child filenames in a scope the operator indexes.
The operator reasonably interprets ? as one Unicode character.
For network impact, online processing is enabled and no independent secret/offline gate blocks the file.
attack_path_facts.context: The scope contributor is explicitly untrusted, and .kcsignore participates in scope and send eligibility. The bypass crosses the operator's declared exclusion boundary before durable archive or approved remote processing.
attack_path_facts.exposure: Operator-mediated local filesystem input; any later network transfer is outbound and separately adapter-approved.
attack_path_facts.identity: The lower-trust contributor controls the pathname and bytes; KCS consumes them with the operator's archive and optional adapter authority.
preconditions: The attacker chooses a precomposed, decomposed, or non-BMP Unicode filename that should satisfy the one-character policy.
The operator runs indexing; a remote sink additionally requires existing online authorization.
attack_path_facts.attacker_control: yes: an in-scope local content contributor directly controls the Unicode filename and file bytes
attack_path_facts.category: Unicode ignore-policy bypass and unintended scope/network eligibility
mitigations: Literal and star rules can independently exclude a file.
Secret classification, offline mode, and adapter approval can prevent a particular network send.
attack_path_facts.auth_scope: local untrusted scope content; optional outbound processing under prior adapter approval
attack_path_facts.impact_surface: scope confidentiality/policy, archive contents, and potential remote data egress
attack_path_facts.target_reach: each crafted direct-child filename within the selected scope
secrets_references: A bypassed file could contain document secrets, but independent secret classification may still hold it.
Adapter credentials are used only if online processing was already authorized.
counterevidence: The bypass does not defeat literal rules, star rules, secret classification, offline mode, or adapter consent.
The contributor generally knows content it supplies, limiting attacker-centric confidentiality impact.
blindspots: The receipts demonstrate eligibility and scan inclusion, but not an end-to-end transmission of a sensitive victim-owned file.
Documented intended semantics for ? are inferred from ordinary character-glob expectations rather than an explicit Unicode contract.
attack_path_facts.rationale: A realistic lower-trust filename bypasses an operator-declared scope boundary and can make excluded bytes durable or remotely eligible. The potential confidentiality/policy impact is High, but the specific ? rule, Unicode name, operator action, and independent gates make likelihood Medium; the matrix yields Medium/P2.

counterevidence: The bypass does not defeat literal rules, star rules, secret classification, offline mode, or adapter consent.
The contributor generally knows content it supplies, limiting attacker-centric confidentiality impact.
proof_gap: The receipts demonstrate eligibility and scan inclusion, but not an end-to-end transmission of a sensitive victim-owned file.
Documented intended semantics for ? are inferred from ordinary character-glob expectations rather than an explicit Unicode contract.
remediation_subsumption_decision: Implement bounded Unicode-scalar wildcard matching; exponential star complexity is tracked separately.
